cowork.notes: Skills and sub-agents use Claude Code markdown formats; artifacts are real files staged in the connected project folder. Skill/agent directories are system-managed: a standalone skill installs via the Save skill flow (zip package), and plugins install from Customize > Plugins (marketplace from a GitHub repo). Plugin-bundled skills work in Claude Chat (web and Desktop) and Cowork alike; hooks and custom sub-agents run ONLY in Cowork and only when packaged inside an installed plugin — a workflow with worker agents must package as Plugin. No verified user-facing memory feature — do not assume Claude Code auto-memory exists here. Verified 2026-09-22: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork, https://claude.com/blog/web-search.

capabilities.skill_install: A standalone skill installs from a zip via the Save skill flow; a plugin (required whenever the workflow has worker agents) installs from Customize > Plugins. Skill and agent directories are system-managed — stage files in the connected project folder and produce one installable package. Start it in a new chat by typing `/` to see available skills and select one, or by describing the task in plain language.
capabilities.context_location: Context files live in the connected project folder; the skill references them by relative path. Supporting reference files can also ship inside the skill package.
capabilities.custom_agents: Yes — as worker sub-agents packaged in an installed plugin (agents/ directory, Claude Code markdown format). The primary Cowork session is the orchestrator and dispatches them; do not design a separate orchestrator agent.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Scheduled tasks run remotely on their chosen cadence even when the desktop app is closed or the computer is asleep, using the connectors and plugins set up in Cowork — but a scheduled run does not inherit connector authorizations from the session that built it. Every connector the workflow touches must be authorized and correctly scoped in the account that runs the task, with permissions pre-granted, since per-task approval prompts can otherwise reappear on each run.
capabilities.web_search: Available, standard on all plans including free.

claude-ai.notes: Claude.ai web/Desktop chat. Guided mode, but skills are still markdown files packaged as a zip and uploaded via Customize > Skills (uploaded skills appear in Chat and Cowork alike), and plugins install from Customize > Plugins on paid plans — generate the skill source files and zip package rather than GUI instruction documents. No standalone sub-agent support (no agent key; plugin sub-agents run only in Cowork): worker agent specs ship inside the skill's agents/ folder and are dispatched by reading that file. Verified 2026-09-22: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude, https://www.xda-developers.com/claude-scheduled-tasks-feature/, https://claude.com/blog/web-search.

capabilities.skill_install: Upload the skill zip under Customize > Skills (appears in Chat and Cowork); plugins install from Customize > Plugins on paid plans. Skills are markdown files packaged as a zip — generate the source files and the zip; GUI steps cover only the upload. Start it in a new chat by typing `/` to see available skills, or by describing the task — Claude applies a matching skill automatically.
capabilities.context_location: A Claude Project's knowledge holds the workflow's context files; start a fresh chat inside the project to run the workflow with them. Small reference material ships inside the skill package.
capabilities.custom_agents: No standalone agent registration. Agent behaviour is written into the skill: an agents/<name>.md file inside the skill package whose body the orchestrator skill dispatches via the platform's Agent tool.
capabilities.unattended_runs: None — Anthropic's own scheduled-task features (Cowork scheduled tasks, Claude Code cloud and desktop scheduled tasks) are separate surfaces from plain Claude.ai chat/Projects, which has no scheduling feature. A workflow that must run unattended is designed as Augmented here, or built on Cowork or Claude Code instead.
capabilities.web_search: Available, standard on all plans including free.

openai-codex.notes: Codex CLI, the Codex tab of the ChatGPT desktop app, and the IDE extension. Skills are folders read from $CWD/.agents/skills up to the repo root, then ~/.agents/skills (user-level default), then /etc/codex/skills; invoke with $skill-name or /skills. Plugins install from a marketplace (Plugins > Add marketplace in the app, or `codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo` in the CLI); ChatGPT and Codex share one plugin directory.

gemini-enterprise.notes: Work/school Google accounts on Standard, Plus, or Pay-as-you-go editions. Skills upload as Markdown or a zip with SKILL.md in the root directory via Skills > + > Upload skill > Import; invoke with @ or /. Skills are not available inside Gemini Enterprise agents. Personal Google accounts use Gemini Spark instead (see gemini-spark).

capabilities.skill_install: Best-effort — not verified this release: Skills upload as Markdown or a zip with SKILL.md in the root directory via Skills > + > Upload skill > Import; invoke with @ or / in a new chat.
capabilities.context_location: Best-effort — not verified this release: no dedicated project/context-file location is documented for this entry; treat any workflow context as shipped inside the skill package until this is verified.
capabilities.custom_agents: Best-effort — not verified this release: skills are not available inside Gemini Enterprise agents, so agent-shaped work and skill-shaped work do not compose on this platform today.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Best-effort — not verified this release: no scheduled or unattended run mechanism is documented for this entry.
capabilities.web_search: Best-effort — not verified this release: web search is available.

gemini-spark.notes: Spark is a mode of the Gemini app (sidebar > Switch to Spark) on the web, the Mac app, and Android/iOS. Personal Google accounts only (not Workspace), Google AI Pro or Ultra, 18+; not available in the EEA, UK, Switzerland, or Nigeria. Skills upload as a SKILL.md or a zip containing one via Skills > Upload; invoke with / in a task or let Spark pick automatically. Skill names must be lowercase-hyphenated.

capabilities.skill_install: Best-effort — not verified this release: Skills upload as a SKILL.md or a zip containing one via Skills > Upload; invoke with / in a new task or let Spark pick automatically.
capabilities.context_location: Best-effort — not verified this release: no dedicated project/context-file location is documented for this entry; treat any workflow context as shipped inside the skill package until this is verified.
capabilities.custom_agents: Best-effort — not verified this release: no custom-agent primitive is documented for Spark.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Best-effort — not verified this release: no scheduled or unattended run mechanism is documented for this entry.
capabilities.web_search: Best-effort — not verified this release: web search is available.

chatgpt.notes: ChatGPT Chat/Work on web, desktop, and mobile. Skills upload as a zip or SKILL.md under Plugins > Skills > Create > Upload from your computer (paid plans except Free/Go; off by default on Enterprise/Edu until an admin enables); invoke with @skill-name in Work. Plugins (any paid plan) install from Plugins > Add marketplace; plugin-bundled skills work across web, desktop, and mobile. Custom GPTs are deprecated — package agent-shaped work as a Workspace Agent with skills attached. Verified 2026-09-22: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001143-chatgpt-workspace-agents-for-enterprise-and-business, https://openai.com/index/introducing-workspace-agents-in-chatgpt/, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10291617-scheduled-tasks-in-chatgpt, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001066-skills-in-chatgpt returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; corroborated via openai.com/academy/skills and developers.openai.com/codex/skills-and-plugins for the @skill-name invocation).

capabilities.skill_install: Upload the skill as a zip or SKILL.md under Plugins > Skills > Create > Upload from your computer (paid plans except Free/Go; off by default on Enterprise/Edu until an admin enables). Invoke with @skill-name in a new chat, or let ChatGPT auto-match it to the task.
capabilities.context_location: Project files in a ChatGPT Project hold the workflow's context; run the workflow in a new chat inside that project. Small reference material ships inside the skill zip.
capabilities.custom_agents: Workspace Agents are the agent primitive (Custom GPTs are deprecated): build one from Agents > Browse templates or Agents > Create with the Agent Builder, then connect tools and skills to it. In research preview for Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Teachers plans as of this verification.
capabilities.unattended_runs: Scheduled tasks exist per account, including event-triggered tasks tied to a connected Gmail, Slack, or GitHub account (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu, and Healthcare workspaces; not Free/Go). A task can access only the connected account and its existing app permissions, so connector authorization must be completed before the first scheduled run.
capabilities.web_search: Available on Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans, including for signed-out users; triggered automatically or manually via the Search tool, subject to plan usage limits.

integration-registries.name: platform-native-connectors
integration-registries.notes: First stop: the platform entry's capabilities. Claude, Cowork, and ChatGPT ship native connectors for common tools; recommend those before any MCP server, API, or CLI.
